plan: Given my value is $9, I need to balance winning with not overpaying. Since this is the first and only round, I don't have historical data to analyze other bidders' tendencies. A common strategy in second-price auctions is to bid your true value. However, with two other rational bidders, they might also bid their value or slightly below. Bidding my value ensures I win if my value is the highest, and I never pay more than my value. I will bid my value to maximize profit in this single round.

[ The optimal strategy in a second-price auction is to bid your true value. This is a dominant strategy, meaning it's the best strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding below my value risks losing a profitable item, while bidding above my value risks winning an item for more than it's worth. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $20. ]
This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with second-price payment. Optimal strategy is to bid your true value. Since there are only two other bidders, I will bid my value to maximize profit.
